tagline: Push-to-talk dictation that lives in your tray.
description: Clean-room rebuild of a BYOK push-to-talk dictation app for Windows and macOS. Widget-first: the tray pill is the app, the window is for settings. Groq Whisper by default, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint supported. Merges the dictation core with the VFlow feature set (transcription log, usage analytics with live cost, WPM, recap notifications, wrap-up) reimplemented fresh. Copyright LaBroi Walton, GPLv3 from commit one, built entirely on LaBroi's personal machine. No code, prose, specs, or assets may be copied from ~/Projects/undertone, ~/Projects/the-peoples-voice-flow, or ~/Projects/OpenWhisp.

stack.hotkeys: uiohook-napi (prebuilt N-API binaries only, npmRebuild false)
stack.packaging: electron-builder (NSIS for Windows, dmg+zip for macOS)

conventions.verify: npm run typecheck, npm run test, and npm run smoke must be green before any commit. Smoke prints SMOKE_RESULT JSON and every subsystem adds a named check.
conventions.stories: Work stories in order. Never set passes true until every acceptance criterion is verified; record how in notes. Stories with needs_human true get built and smoke-verified, then their human step is appended to HANDOFF.md and work continues.
conventions.commits: One commit per story minimum, prefixed with the story id. git pull --rebase before every commit. After changing prd.json run npm run roadmap.
conventions.cleanRoom: Never open or copy from the undertone, the-peoples-voice-flow, or OpenWhisp repos. Concepts yes, artifacts no. If blocked without them, stop and ask LaBroi.
conventions.style: No em dashes or spaced hyphens as clause separators anywhere. Night studio design tokens only, amber reserved for live states. The product name is always lowercase murmur in every user-visible surface, even at sentence start.

stories.title: Smoke harness

MURMUR_SMOKE_FORCE_FAIL=1 injects a failing check: ok false, exit 1. No mic, network, or key touched; per-check 10s timeout, 60s harness kill switch.

stories.title: Tray shell, single instance, widget-first window
stories.description: Tray (menu bar on macOS) icon with menu: Open Murmur, pause dictation, Quit. Clicking the tray opens the settings window. Single instance lock: a second launch focuses the first. Closing the window hides it, the app lives in the tray. macOS runs without a Dock icon by default with a setting to show it.
acceptance: Smoke check tray reports the tray and window created
Second launch exits immediately and the first instance shows its window
Window close hides the window and the process stays alive
Quit is only offered from the tray menu and exits cleanly
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: smoke checks tray, singleInstanceLock, settingsWindow, and widgetLifecycle (close hides, process survives) all green. Live CLI test: second launch exited in 1s while the first stayed alive and took the handoff. Quit exists only in the tray menu; window close is intercepted and hides. macOS runs menu-bar resident with Dock hidden. Dev builds use an isolated murmur-dev userData so the lock and settings never collide with the installed legacy app (found live: the old Murmur.app held the Murmur lock). LaBroi reported 2026-09-12: clicking Open murmur in the tray appeared to do nothing. Root cause: with the Dock icon hidden murmur is a macOS accessory app, and show() plus focus() on the BrowserWindow does not raise an accessory app's window above the active app; the window opened buried behind other windows (confirmed live: the window sat at screen center under Chrome while the tray click looked dead, and a real app activation surfaced it instantly). Fix 2026-09-13: showSettingsWindow calls app.focus({ steal: true }) on darwin after show. Verified: typecheck, 278 unit tests, smoke green 3 consecutive runs (settingsWindow, widgetLifecycle, tray checks included). Remaining live: LaBroi confirms a tray Open murmur click raises the window above other apps in the installed build (HANDOFF.md).

acceptance: Unit tests cover defaults, merge, unknown-key preservation, and corrupt-file recovery with backup
Smoke check settings passes
The plaintext key never appears in any log file or renderer payload (grep the userData logs after a smoke run that sets a key)
Key round-trips through safeStorage encrypt and decrypt
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 18 new unit tests (merge semantics incl. unknown-key preservation, corrupt-file recovery with .bak, atomic saves, keystore round-trip with injected cipher, no-plaintext-on-disk, masked status). Smoke checks settings and secureKey green: real safeStorage round-trip of a probe key then cleared. Leak scan: probe plaintext appears zero times in smoke output, userData tree, or settings.json; key lives only in key.enc encrypted. Renderer receives only {present, masked}.

stories.title: Global hotkeys: hold and toggle
stories.description: uiohook-napi global listener with two modes: hold-to-talk (press starts, release stops) and toggle (tap starts, tap stops). Bindings are configurable in settings with a capture UI that records the pressed combo. Sensible per-platform defaults. Debounced state machine so key repeat and rapid taps never double-fire.
acceptance: Combo parse and format helpers are unit tested
Hold and toggle state machines are unit tested for press, release, repeat, and rapid-tap sequences
Smoke check hotkeys registers and unregisters the listener
Rebinding from the settings UI takes effect without restart
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05 (17 unit tests, smoke hotkeys and hotkeysRebind). Live verified by LaBroi 2026-09-05: captured Ctrl+Alt from the settings UI with no restart and dictated with it end to end. Later hardening: modifier-only chords via code-tracked dispatcher, safe-binding rule (bare typing keys invalid), capture via the global hook with window fallback.

stories.title: Recording pipeline with warm mic
stories.description: A hidden audio renderer captures the mic to 16kHz mono WAV. The stream is pre-armed (warm mic) with a short ring buffer so the first syllable is never clipped. Handles sleep, resume, and device changes by re-arming automatically. Cancel discards audio. Smoke drives the pipeline with a synthetic source.
acceptance: Smoke check recording produces a valid WAV header and nonzero samples from a synthetic source
WAV encoder is unit tested (header fields, sample counts, mono 16k)
Resume and device-change events re-arm the stream without an app restart
Live: LaBroi confirms the first word of a fast press-and-speak is captured
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 8 WAV unit tests (encoder header fields, byte lengths, clamping, downsample 48k to 16k, parse rejects garbage). Smoke recording check green 3 consecutive runs: hidden capture window with synthetic oscillator produces valid 16k mono PCM16 WAV with pre-roll included, nonzero peak. Smoke recordingRearm green: main-driven rearm round trip re-arms the graph. powerMonitor resume triggers rearm; a dead track re-arms itself. Found and fixed: sandboxed preloads cannot load shared rollup chunks, channel literals now live inline per preload. Remaining live: first-syllable capture with a real mic (HANDOFF.md). LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-07: fast press-and-speak captures the first word. LaBroi reported 2026-09-09: after sleep and wake (both Mac and PC) the hotkey no longer captures audio. Root cause: the resume re-arm was single-shot with every failure path unhandled; getUserMedia right after wake commonly rejects or hangs while the OS audio stack re-enumerates, one failed attempt left the mic dead until restart, and a silently stalled graph (Windows modern standby) or a killed capture renderer had no detection at all. Fix 2026-09-09 (v0.1.5): chunk-liveness watchdog in the recorder (a healthy graph delivers chunks continuously; a stall re-arms with retry until chunks flow, hung attempts abandoned via a generation counter), all arm paths guarded, and main reloads the capture renderer on render-process-gone with escalating backoff. Review gate confirmed seven findings, all fixed: teardown now clears shared state synchronously before any await (a slow close could null a successor's live graph and orphan its stream), a recording in progress survives graph death as rate-tagged segments so a mid-take outage never loses captured speech, getUserMedia is acquired before the AudioContext so abandoned hung attempts cannot exhaust the per-page context cap, ready is decoupled from first-arm success, the revive backoff escalates by crash spacing instead of resetting on every ready, the recovery smoke check requires an outage ack so it cannot pass on an unbroken graph, and the docs no longer claim platform verification that has not happened. Verified after fixes: 8 liveness unit tests; smoke checks recordingRecovery (graph killed silently plus two forced arm failures, recovers unaided) and recordingRevive (renderer crashed, revives and records) green 3 consecutive runs. LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-12: after real sleep and wake on both the Mac and the PC, the hotkey captures audio normally again. Story fully complete.

Timer ticks while recording and resets between sessions

stories.title: Transcription provider
stories.description: A provider interface with Groq Whisper as the default implementation, model configurable. Any OpenAI-compatible audio transcriptions endpoint works via base URL, model, and key settings. Timeouts, one retry on network error, and on final failure the WAV is saved to a recovery folder and the overlay shows the error. Audio is never lost.
acceptance: Unit tests with a mocked fetch cover success, 4xx, 5xx, timeout, and the single retry
Smoke check provider passes in mock mode
A failed transcription leaves a playable WAV in userData recovery and surfaces the error state
Live: LaBroi runs one real dictation against Groq with a real key
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05 (9 provider unit tests, recovery tests, provider and dictationLoop smoke). Live verified by LaBroi 2026-09-05: real Groq key saved and connection test green, real dictations transcribed and delivered.

stories.title: Insertion at the cursor
stories.description: Final text lands at the cursor in the focused app: save clipboard, set text, send the platform paste keystroke, restore the clipboard. macOS uses osascript keystroke (no compiled helper), Windows uses a no-compile keystroke path. A copy-only fallback setting exists. Insertion must never steal or shift focus.
acceptance: Clipboard save and restore logic is unit tested, including non-text clipboard content left untouched on failure
Smoke check insertion initializes the platform strategy
Copy-only mode puts the text on the clipboard and skips the keystroke
Live: LaBroi verifies insertion in three real apps per platform without focus loss
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 7 unit tests on the pure restore plan (clean restore, empty original, non-text payload untouched, user copy mid-insertion wins) and the platform keystroke builders (osascript cmd+v, powershell SendKeys, null elsewhere). Smoke insertion check runs the copy path end to end and restores the user clipboard; keystrokes are never fired in smoke by design. Paste failure fails open to copied, so text is never lost. Copy-only mode is a setting (insertion.mode). Remaining live: paste into three real apps per platform without focus loss (HANDOFF.md). LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-07: insertion confirmed in real apps, focus intact, clipboard restored. Fix 2026-09-07 (LaBroi field report: clipboard overwritten by dictations): the restore is now full fidelity. The old design skipped restoring whenever the clipboard held any non-text flavor, which on macOS is nearly every real copy (screenshots outright, and even plain text carries extra flavors), so restores rarely fired. The clipboard is now captured wholesale (all items, all MIME flavors, materialized before we overwrite, 32MB cap) and written back atomically after the paste settles; text is the fallback, a mid-insertion user copy still wins, and a screenshot copied before dictating now survives. Verified: rewritten planRestore unit tests plus the insertion smoke check now does a live capture-and-restore round trip. LaBroi reported 2026-09-12: a dictation transcribed and recorded to history but never appeared in the target app. Root cause: the paste keystroke posts the Cmd+V event and resolves, but the target app reads the pasteboard only when it processes that event, and there is no OS signal for the read (reading does not bump the change count). The 250ms inline settle lost that race on a loaded system (a macOS update was installing), so the clipboard restore landed before the app's paste read and the paste delivered stale content. Fix 2026-09-13: settle raised to 1500ms and moved to a background task so the inserted feedback stays immediate; insertText awaits any pending restore before capturing, so back-to-back dictations cannot interleave a restore with a fresh capture; planRestore's mid-dictation copy protection is unchanged. Verified: typecheck, 278 unit tests, smoke green 3 consecutive runs (insertion and dictationLoop checks included). Remaining live: LaBroi confirms a real dictation pastes into a busy app and the prior clipboard comes back about 1.5s later (HANDOFF.md). Review gate 2026-09-13 confirmed two findings, both fixed: the backgrounded restore swallowed errors silently (now logged loud via console.error, and the settle's clipboard read guarded like capture's), and a fast follow-on dictation could stall up to 1.5s awaiting the pending settle (insertText now flushes a sleeping settle before awaiting, so the wait is milliseconds; the predecessor's paste has had a full record-and-transcribe round to land by then). Re-verified after fixes: typecheck, 278 unit tests, smoke green.

stories.title: Silence never inserts text
stories.description: An energy gate (RMS threshold plus minimum voiced duration) short-circuits before upload, and a transcript sanity filter (empty, whitespace, known Whisper hallucination phrases) short-circuits after. Either path shows a quiet no-speech state and inserts nothing.
acceptance: Unit tests: silent buffer, breath noise, and real-speech synthetic buffers classify correctly
Hallucination phrase list is data-driven and tested
Smoke check silence passes
Live: LaBroi holds the hotkey in silence and nothing is inserted
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 8 unit tests (pure silence, breath-level noise, speech bursts, one-loud-click rejected by the 200ms voiced minimum; empty, punctuation-only, and known phrases flagged case and punctuation insensitively; real dictations containing a phrase pass). Hallucination list is data-driven in shared/hallucinations.json. Both guards wired into dictationStop (energy gate before upload, sanity filter after) and covered by smoke silenceGuard. Remaining live: hold the hotkey in silence, expect the quiet no speech state (HANDOFF.md). Update 2026-09-06 (LaBroi field report of trailing injections): a two-layer tail defense shipped: deterministic stripping of trailing artifactTails sentences (a strict never-genuinely-spoken subset; the reviewer blocked a first version that would have eaten real thank-you sign-offs, and history now records the transcript exactly as heard), plus the polish validator rejecting outputs that end on a hallucination phrase the input did not end on. LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-06: the silence hold is good, nothing inserts. Update 2026-09-07 night: LaBroi caught a live injection; history showed a fabricated trailing Okay in the RAW transcript, so ASR-born. Genuinely dictatable words stay off the deterministic strip lists per the iron law; instead the cleanup model now carries a disconnected-trailing-filler rule (judgment layer, fails open) plus a never-introduce-em-dashes rule after it inserted one into his text. Validator test confirms a dropped trailing filler passes.

stories.title: Format spec and shared test vectors
stories.description: shared/format-spec.json defines deterministic formatter rules: filler removal, sentence capitalization, terminal punctuation, spoken punctuation and newline commands, self-correction handling, and a numbers mode. shared/test-vectors.json holds input and expected pairs. A pure-function formatter implements the spec and vitest runs every vector.
acceptance: Every vector in shared/test-vectors.json passes
The formatter is a pure function with no IO
Spec rules are documented inside format-spec.json itself
Adding a vector with an unimplemented rule fails the suite (proving vectors drive behavior)
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: shared/format-spec.json documents every rule and the pipeline order inline; 26 vectors in shared/test-vectors.json all pass through the vector-runner test (fillers, spoken punctuation attach and capitalize, scratch-that sentence scoping, numbers digits and words modes, terminal punctuation, level off and light behavior). Vectors proved they drive behavior during development: two initially failed and forced a pipeline reorder (spoken punctuation before scratch-that). formatTranscript is a pure function wired into dictationStop; smoke dictationLoop now asserts the formatted output lands.

stories.title: Provider and model controls
stories.description: Settings UI over the provider fields that have existed since US-010: swap the speech and cleanup models from Groq suggestions or type any model id, point the base URL at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, a proxy, a local server), and reset to Groq defaults. Values apply on the next dictation with no restart because the transcriber reads settings per call. Requested by LaBroi 2026-09-05.
acceptance: Base URL, speech model, and cleanup model are editable fields; both model fields offer Groq suggestions while accepting any typed id
Edits persist through the settings store and apply to the next dictation without restart
Reset restores the Groq defaults
The connection test exercises whatever base URL and key are configured
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-05: provider panel with base URL, speech model, and cleanup model fields (Groq suggestions via datalist plus free text), commit-on-blur, reset-to-defaults. Typecheck and 114 unit tests green; settings capture screenshot verified the panel renders. Smoke rerun green 2026-09-05 once the session unlocked (the wedge was environmental, confirmed by a minimal Electron probe failing identically). All criteria verified.

stories.title: LLM formatter that fails open
stories.description: Optional cleanup pass through a Groq-hosted chat model (configurable) with levels off, light, and full. Strict system prompt plus output validation: length-ratio bounds, no meta chatter, and dictated instructions are transcribed literally, never obeyed. Any error, timeout, or validation failure returns the deterministic pre-formatted text.
acceptance: Mocked-LLM unit tests: API error, timeout, chatty preamble, refusal, and an embedded instruction like a request to delete text all fail open to the deterministic output
Prompt-injection vectors in shared/test-vectors.json pass (dictations containing instructions come out as literal text)
Smoke check formatter passes in mock mode
Level off skips the LLM entirely
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 13 unit tests on validatePolish and polishTranscript with mocked fetch (API error, network throw, timeout via AbortController, chatty preamble, refusal, preamble-colon line, quote-wrapper stripping, length drift both directions, obeyed-instruction detection via length guard, malformed body). Three prompt-injection vectors added to shared/test-vectors.json and passing (dictated instructions transcribed literally). Smoke llmFormatter green: clean accepts, chatty and 500 and obeyed all fail open. Wiring: runs only at Full level, never in smoke, never without a key, single attempt with 8s cap, falls back to deterministic output on any failure; off and light skip the LLM entirely. Uses the configured cleanup model and base URL per dictation.

stories.title: Custom dictionary
stories.description: A user dictionary of proper nouns and replacement pairs applied deterministically after transcription and offered to the LLM as hints without leaking. Settings UI lists, adds, edits, and removes entries.
acceptance: Vectors cover replacements, casing of proper nouns, and word-boundary safety
Leak test: a large dictionary plus an unrelated dictation never injects dictionary words into output
Dictionary hint text never appears in inserted output in any mocked-LLM failure mode
Settings UI round-trips entries to the store
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: applyDictionary is pure, word-boundary safe (conditional boundaries so c++ style terms work), case-insensitive in, exact casing out, longest phrase wins, regex-escaped, type-resilient against hand-edited settings. Four shared vectors including brand casing surviving sentence-start capitalization via enforceDictionaryCasing, which runs last in the pipeline. LLM hint via dictionaryHint with a Preferred spellings leak sentinel; hint echo can never reach output (unit tested). Settings UI editor with add and remove. Smoke dictionary check covers replacement, boundary safety, and the store round trip. First story through the independent review gate: reviewer confirmed two real findings (sentence-start casing clobber; wrong-typed entries could throw uncaught, wedging the overlay in processing and losing the dictation), both fixed with tests, and the whole formatting stage now fails open to the raw transcript. 24 dictionary-related unit tests among 154 total.

stories.title: Text expansions
stories.description: Spoken trigger phrases expand to saved snippets after formatting (for example a spoken email trigger inserts the full address). Managed in settings with collision rules: longest trigger wins, one expansion per utterance position.
acceptance: Vectors cover expansion, longest-match collision, and no-match passthrough
Settings UI round-trips expansions to the store
Expansions apply after the formatter so triggers are matched on clean text
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: applyExpansions is single-pass (snippet content never rescanned, so no recursive expansion), longest-trigger-wins at a position, non-overlapping, boundary-safe via the shared matcher, case-insensitive triggers with verbatim snippets, type-resilient. 8 unit tests plus 3 shared vectors (post-formatting trigger match, longest wins, no rescan); vector runner now mirrors the full pipeline order. Settings editor via generalized PairAdd; smoke expansions check covers apply, boundary, and store round trip. Review gate round two: reviewer confirmed the snippet editor could not produce the multi-line sign-offs the feature advertises (fixed with a textarea, Enter for newline, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter submits); its matchAll typing finding was verified not applicable on this toolchain (typecheck green on TS 7) and recorded rather than dropped.

stories.title: History: append-only log and home transcription view
stories.description: Every completed session appends a JSONL event to userData: timestamp, duration, raw text, final text, word count, WPM, and cost estimate. The home view of the settings window is the transcription log grouped by date with copy buttons, live updates as sessions land, a retention setting, and clear-all.
acceptance: Append, read, date grouping, and corrupt-line tolerance are unit tested
Smoke check history writes and reads a synthetic session end to end
The home view updates live when a session completes (IPC event test)
Copy button places the final text on the clipboard, retention prunes old entries, clear-all empties the log
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: append-only JSONL log with corrupt-line tolerance, retention pruning (0 keeps forever), atomic rewrites, clear-all; 10 log and helper unit tests (grouping in local time, DST-safe day boundary, wpm math, shape guard). Home view is the default tab: day-grouped entries with time, words, wpm, per-entry copy via a main-process clipboard handler, live appends, retention select, clear all; visually verified via capture. Smoke history check green. Review gate round three confirmed three findings, all fixed: IPC listener leak on tab switches (preload now returns an unsubscribe, used in effect cleanup), unbounded live-append growth (capped at 500 to match the list handler), and prune running on every settings save (now only on actual retention changes); plus hardening applied so transcript events broadcast only to the settings window, never the overlay or audio windows.

stories.title: Usage analytics and live cost card
stories.description: Aggregations over the event log power an analytics page: minutes dictated, words, sessions, and daily activity chart, plus a monthly usage card with a live cost estimate computed from shared/rates.json. Rates are verified against the provider pricing page and the check date is recorded in the file.
acceptance: Aggregation unit tests cover month boundaries, empty logs, and multi-day ranges
Cost math matches shared/rates.json exactly and rates carry a verified-on date sourced from the provider pricing page
Analytics page renders from a seeded log in smoke
Usage card updates after a new session lands
stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 9 aggregation unit tests (month and today boundaries local-time and DST safe, zero-filled chronological 14-day series, empty log, cost math incl. the Groq 10-second ASR billing minimum, fallback rates, no compounding rounding). Analytics tab renders monthly card with live cost estimate, 14-day chart (cream emphasis, amber stays reserved), lifetime totals; summary computed in main so transcripts never reach the renderer for charts; smoke analytics check green. Review gate CRITICAL catch: the llama cleanup defaults had been decommissioned by Groq on 2026-08-16, confirmed against console.groq.com/docs/deprecations, meaning the cleanup pass had been silently failing open for all users; rates.json, defaults, UI suggestions, and docs repointed to openai/gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b (rates from the primary models page), plus an automatic settings migration for existing profiles. Also fixed per review: per-day minutes rounding no longer compounds (regression test added). Lesson recorded: verify against primary sources, secondary roundups quoted stale tables. Update 2026-09-06: lifetime avg wpm stat added and an 18-week GitHub-style activity heatmap (the mat) added to analytics at LaBroi's request, cream intensity ladder with today outlined, summary span widened to 126 days. Update 2026-09-06 round two: the wall gained GitHub parity at LaBroi's request: month and weekday labels, per-day hover with date and words, a period word total, and a year picker back to the first session (new analytics:heatmap channel with a pure heatmap() range function, smoke-checked). Earned belt colors joined the accents (past colors stay earned) and drive both the wall fill and a gui accent variable tinting chart bars and gate fills; amber stays reserved for live states. Update 2026-09-07: period semantics corrected per LaBroi: the default view is now named lifetime (first dictation through today, padded to a year minimum) and calendar years show only themselves; the ambiguous last year label is gone, today is outlined in any period containing it, and the wall scrollbar is styled quiet on ink. Update 2026-09-07 later: wall default fill switched from cream to a vibrant orange token (cream read as the white belt color), and dark fills like the black belt invert the wall (light empty squares, activity darkens) via a luminance check, so no earned color can vanish into the ink.

stories.title: Post-session WPM in the overlay

stories.title: Progression engine: BJJ belts and stripes
stories.description: The rank system LaBroi specced 2026-09-05: adult Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu belts, verified against the IBJJF General Graduation System (researched via EXA 2026-09-05). Ladder: no belt, then white, blue, purple, brown, black (four stripes each), black belt degrees 1 to 6, coral red-and-black at 7th, coral red-and-white at 8th, red at 9th; the 10th stays reserved for the pioneers and is unearnable, on purpose. shared/ranks.json encodes every rank with a lifetime-words threshold, a minimum-active-days gate honoring the spirit of IBJJF time-in-grade minimums (2 years at blue, 1.5 at purple, 1 at brown, 3 to 5 per black degree, scaled to app time), and a title. A pure engine computes rank, stripes, progress, and promotion history deterministically from the event log. Balancing lives entirely in the JSON. Founder provision (LaBroi, 2026-09-05): the 10th degree red belt is the Founder belt, held by LaBroi alone, exactly as the real 10th was reserved for the pioneers of the art; every other user tops out at the 9th. v1 recognizes a local founder marker (honor system, like all local ranks); the Phase 2 cloud tier makes it verifiable.
acceptance: shared/ranks.json carries the full adult ladder with words thresholds, active-day minimums, and titles; the 10th degree is present but marked unearnable

Promotion requires BOTH gates: a words burst without enough active days does not skip a belt

stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-06: shared/ranks.json carries the full adult ladder (31 earnable ranks plus the founder-only 10th with null thresholds) with monotonicity enforced by test; computeProgress is pure with dual gates, dated promotions, founder short-circuit, and 12 tests including anti-burst in both directions, same-day dedup, order independence, and the unearnable 10th. ranks:progress IPC computes in main with the founder file marker; smoke ranks check green. Review gate finding fixed: day keys are now STORED on each event at record time and used across ranks, analytics, recap, and wrap-up, so a timezone change can never re-bucket history and demote an earned belt (regression test added). Update 2026-09-06: belt promotions now notify once each (highest new rank per batch, announced-state file), closing the silent-white-belt gap LaBroi hit on his first dictation.

stories.title: Brand gold: the icon's metal becomes the primary
stories.description: LaBroi direction 2026-09-07: the logo's gold becomes the app's primary color for headlines and attention highlights. Design resolution: a two-metal system. Burnished brand gold (#d9a441, the icon family at label luminance) colors every panel eyebrow, the murmur wordmark, and the active nav tab; signal amber stays reserved for live states and always outshines the brand metal, so recording still pops; founder gold stays identity-only. Everything else stays quiet cream.
acceptance: A brand token exists and colors micro-labels, the wordmark, and the active nav tab
Signal amber remains exclusively for live/active states and is brighter than brand gold
The design law in CLAUDE.md records the three-metal hierarchy
LaBroi blesses the look
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-07, automated criteria verified: token added, three surfaces recolored, design lint and all gates green, CLAUDE.md law updated. Awaiting LaBroi's visual blessing. LaBroi blessed the gold in the installed app, 2026-09-07 night.

stories.title: Settings color previews and accent clarity
stories.description: LaBroi requests 2026-09-07: live swatches next to the accent and theme dropdowns so the choice is visible before it lands, and copy making clear the accent is the app-wide default while the activity wall keeps its own picker. Design counsel: the 14-day chart already follows the global accent, so it gets no separate picker (one default plus one showcase override is the whole hierarchy); themes stay a small curated set of rooms with rank gates rather than one per belt, since accents already carry belt personalization.

A two-tone swatch beside the theme select previews the theme's ink and panel from data
The accent row copy states it is the app-wide default and points at the wall's own picker
LaBroi blesses the look

stories.title: Repo public readiness
stories.description: Full audit of the working tree and all git history before lbwalton/murmur flips public: secrets, personal data, legal references, contamination, and front-door quality. Audit ran 2026-09-07 over every commit, blob, reflog entry, and dangling object.
acceptance: No secrets, credentials, transcripts, or binaries anywhere in history (verified clean)
The signing key id and fixture emails are out of the current tree
History is rewritten to remove the private legal note and key id, re-scanned clean, and force-pushed while still private, with LaBroi's explicit approval
package.json carries repository, homepage, and bugs; the flip-day checklist in HANDOFF is executed when LaBroi says go
stories.notes: Audit found exactly two history items needing a rewrite: a private lawyer note in HANDOFF across 49 commits, and the signing key id across 12. Neither is a usable credential and no case number exists anywhere. Tree fixes landed 2026-09-07; the filter-repo rewrite awaits LaBroi's go, cheap while private, impossible after. Completed 2026-09-08: LaBroi approved the rewrite; filter-repo removed both items; an adversarial rescan of all 62 commits, 519 blobs, reflog, and dangling objects returned clean to publish; the old remote was archived private and a fresh lbwalton/murmur received the clean history (avoiding GitHub's retained-object leak via Actions logs); a fresh clone from GitHub re-verified zero residue; the repo flipped PUBLIC with description, topics, Dependabot alerts, automated security fixes, secret scanning with push protection, and branch protection; release v0.1.0 published with the notarized dmg, mac zip, three Windows installers, and updater manifests.

stories.title: murmur Pro: offline license keys and the unlock flow
stories.description: The one-time Pro unlock, built on the launch-day payments decision: Stripe Managed Payments (merchant of record) sells via a Payment Link, and murmur issues its OWN license keys, ed25519 signatures the app verifies offline against a public key shipped in shared/pro.json. No licensing server, no phone-home, nothing to outlive the company. The private signing key lives only on LaBroi's machine; scripts/issue-license.js signs a key per order. Settings gains a murmur pro section: paste and activate, supporter status when active, a Get Pro button when the Payment Link URL is configured. Cosmetics stay earned, never bought; Pro is support and convenience.
acceptance: A signed key activates offline and survives restarts; tampered, forged, and malformed keys are rejected, covered by tests and a smoke check
The private signing key exists nowhere in the repo or its history
Settings shows the pro section: activation when unlicensed, supporter status when licensed, and the buy button only when a Payment Link is configured
LaBroi creates the Stripe Payment Link ($49 list, $39 founders window) and its URL lands in shared/pro.json
A real end-to-end purchase issues a key that activates in a shipped build
LaBroi decides the first Pro conveniences; nothing already free gets taken away
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-08, automated criteria verified: verify and reject paths tested (ephemeral keypairs, six cases), smoke check guards the reject path, keypair generated on LaBroi's machine at ~/.config/murmur/license-signing.pem (chmod 600), public key committed in shared/pro.json. Awaiting LaBroi: Payment Link creation, pricing confirmation, first Pro conveniences, live purchase test. 2026-09-08: Stripe configured end to end in LaBroi's session: product murmur Pro at 49 dollars (Downloadable Software tax category), Payment Link with Managed Payments enabled (merchant of record, tax handled, sold through Link) and promotion codes allowed, coupon Founders (10 dollars off once) with code FOUNDERS. The link is live in shared/pro.json, so the Get Pro button ships in the next release. The issue script now appends every key to a private ledger at ~/.config/murmur/issued-licenses.jsonl for reissue and support lookups. Remaining human steps: pricing window decision on when FOUNDERS retires, first Pro conveniences, and the live purchase test.

stories.title: Pro conveniences: provider profiles and the founders promise
stories.description: The first real Pro contents, decided by LaBroi 2026-09-08. Provider profiles: save endpoint, models, and the matching API key under a name and switch in one click; keys move as encrypted blob copies, plaintext never surfaces; the free single setup is untouched. Standing benefits: early access windows in official builds, priority support, SUPPORTERS.md credit. Founders promise: every founders-window buyer holds a permanent ten percent discount on all future paid products (cloud subscription, paid iOS), carried as a signed founder flag in their license key and honored at future checkouts.
acceptance: Profiles save, apply, and delete via Pro-gated IPC; without a license every operation refuses (smoke-checked) and the free provider setup is untouched
Applying a profile swaps endpoint, models, and key together; a profile without a key leaves the active key alone
The license payload carries the founder flag through signing and verification, covered by tests, and settings shows founding member status with the discount promise
docs and SUPPORTERS.md record what Pro includes and the founders policy
LaBroi live-verifies profiles after activating his own key
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-08, automated criteria verified: gates green with the new profilesGate smoke check and founder flag tests. Live verification rides LaBroi's test purchase: issue his key with --founder, activate, then save and switch a profile.

stories.title: Smart lists: spoken structure becomes real structure, behind a toggle
stories.description: At Full formatting with the new Smart lists toggle ON (default off; today's behavior is untouched when off), dictations that speak a sequence (first, then, then) come out as a numbered list, and item run-ons (I need to pack socks, shirts, shoes) come out as dash bullets, one item per line; plain prose stays prose. Implemented in the polish prompt plus validator allowances for list shapes (a colon intro line before list lines is legitimate, list markers are excluded from the length sanity counts), and deterministic spoken commands (bullet point, next item, numbered list) in shared/format-spec.json gated by the same toggle. Output uses plain dash and number prefixes only, no markdown assumptions. The formatter still fails open: a rejected polish falls back to the deterministic text, and the deterministic path never depends on the model. Decided with LaBroi 2026-09-13.
acceptance: Smart lists toggle in settings, default off; with it off, formatter output and the polish prompt are unchanged from today (unit-tested)

With it on, the polish prompt carries the list instructions and validatePolish accepts a well-formed list transformation (colon intro plus dash or numbered lines) while still rejecting chatter, length abuse, and injected content (unit tests cover accept and reject cases)
Spoken commands (bullet point, next item) produce list lines deterministically at Full with the toggle on, specced in shared/format-spec.json and covered in shared/test-vectors.json
Docs updated: what the toggle does, both list shapes with examples
Live: LaBroi dictates a packing list and a first-second-third sequence; both render as lists in a plain text field and in a markdown-aware app
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-13. Toggle formatting.smartLists (default false) in settings schema, UI row in the dictation panel, wired through dictationStop and maybePolish. Deterministic side: listCommands in shared/format-spec.json (bullet point, next bullet, next item map to newline dash lines) applied in the spokenPunctuation stage only when the toggle is on; ensureTerminal never staples a period onto a final list line; 5 new shared vectors in test-vectors.json cover on, off-by-default, synonyms, leading-command, and prose-unchanged cases. Polish side: SMART_LISTS_PROMPT appended to the system prompt only when on; validatePolish gains a smartLists opt that allows a colon intro directly over list lines and excludes list markers from the length-ratio word counts; chatter, colon-over-prose, and length-drift rejections unchanged and re-tested with the flag on. Verified: typecheck clean, 288 unit tests green (5 new vectors, 5 new llm tests), smoke green. One test expectation corrected during build: a Cleaned text colon intro rejects as meta chatter (the earlier guard), so the preamble-rule case uses a neutral colon intro. Remaining live criterion: LaBroi dictates both list shapes into a plain text field and a markdown app (HANDOFF.md). Review gate 2026-09-13 confirmed one finding, fixed: the no-period-on-list-endings rule in ensureTerminal ran unconditionally, so a raw transcript already starting a line with a dash would have changed output with the toggle off; the rule is now gated on smartLists and two parity vectors lock both directions. Re-verified after the fix: typecheck clean, 290 unit tests, smoke green.

stories.title: Provider connections: mix engines, see real costs
stories.description: BYOK grows from one shared endpoint to two connection slots: a speech-to-text connection and a polish connection, each with its own base URL, safeStorage-encrypted key, and model dropdown, so Groq transcription can pair with a DeepSeek polish. Curated launch presets: Groq (default), OpenAI, Mistral (Voxtral), and a Local preset (speaches or faster-whisper-server for STT, Ollama or LM Studio for polish); polish-only presets: DeepSeek, Cerebras, OpenRouter. The custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint field stays for everything else. Gemini and non-OpenAI-compatible STT APIs (Deepgram, AssemblyAI, ElevenLabs) are deferred. A provider catalog at shared/provider-catalog.json carries models, rates, free-tier and billing nuances, and a verified-on date per fact; a weekly scheduled GitHub Action re-verifies rates against vendor primary sources and opens a PR only when a number changed, so LaBroi approves every number that ships. The app bundles the catalog and refreshes it from the repo at launch (on by default with a settings off switch; a read-only file fetch to the same GitHub host the updater already contacts, carrying no user data). Setup shows an estimated cost per 1,000 dictated words computed locally from the user's own average pace in history (fallback 130 wpm before history exists) next to each model, labeled with the verified-on date. Free tier keeps the full setup, dropdowns, and cost estimates; Pro adds saved profiles and one-click switching (US-042). Decided with LaBroi 2026-09-13.
acceptance: Two connection slots (STT, polish) with per-slot base URL, encrypted key, and model; existing single-provider setups migrate automatically and behave exactly as today (migration unit-tested)
Curated presets fill base URLs and model dropdowns from shared/provider-catalog.json; the custom endpoint path still accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL
Cost per 1k words is computed locally from history average wpm plus catalog rates, shown per model with the rates' verified-on date; no usage data leaves the machine

provider-catalog.json exists with per-fact verified-on dates; a weekly GitHub Action re-verifies rates against vendor primary sources and opens a PR only on change; the app itself never scrapes or calls vendors for pricing
Catalog refresh at launch: latest catalog fetched from the repo with bundled fallback, on by default, off switch in settings, documented; failures log and never block dictation

Billing nuance notes render in setup: Groq free tier bills nothing and rate-limits instead (developer tier bills only past 50 cents), OpenAI API has no free tier, Mistral Voxtral rates, DeepSeek peak and off-peak rates, Local is free
Docs: per-provider setup page (base URL, key, model ids, rates with verified-on dates) for every preset, per the documentation product-surface rule
Live: LaBroi pairs Groq STT with a different provider's polish and dictates end to end
